title: Ramified finite-free scalar systems and their coherent exceptional transpose
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, uniformizers $\pi,v$, and ramification index $e\ge1$, so $\pi S=v^eS$. Put $A_n=R/\pi^n$, $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with a fixed compactification $f=pj$, $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Work on fixed small pro-etale skeletons [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For $D=R,S$ and $W=X,Y$, let $\mathscr N_D(W)$ be the full subcategory of the ordinary unbounded derived category of strict semilinear systems over $(A_n)_W$ or $(B_n)_W$ consisting of normalized systems with levels in $D^b_{ctf}$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Normalized means that every transition-adjoint $N_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to N_n$, or its $B$ analogue, is invertible for $m\ge n$. Write $\mathsf F_D\dashv\mathsf E_D$ for the specified compact-support/exceptional system adjunction, and $\epsilon_D^{\rm sys}$ for its counit, with the simultaneous enriched realizations of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization, lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates]. The $S$ functors here are retained at the levels $en$, with composite quotient transitions.

Derived scalar extension along $((A_n)_W)_n\to((B_n)_W)_n$ gives a functor
$$\mathsf T_W^{(e)}:\mathscr N_R(W)\longrightarrow\mathscr N_S(W),\qquad (\mathsf T_W^{(e)}N)_n=N_n\otimes^L_{A_n}B_n.$$
Its transition-adjoints are tensor reassociation followed by the scalar extension of the transition-adjoints of $N$. The canonical proper coefficient projection followed by the open-extension tensor identification gives a natural isomorphism of derived-system functors
$$\alpha^{\rm sys}:\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}\mathsf F_R\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf F_S\mathsf T_X^{(e)}.$$
It is realized by the simultaneous section constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Its evaluation is the canonical finite-free compact-support comparison $\alpha_n$ of [lem-coef-finite-free-compact-composition, lem-coef-finite-free-extension], independent of a basis, whose underlying map in a single $R$-basis of $S$ reduced at every level is finite-sum distributivity. These comparisons commute with all quotient squares $A_m\to A_n$, $B_m\to B_n$.

For every $N\in\mathscr N_R(Y)$ the specified system transpose of
$$\lambda_N=\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}(\epsilon^{\rm sys}_{R,N})\circ(\alpha^{\rm sys}_{\mathsf E_RN})^{-1}:
\mathsf F_S\mathsf T_X^{(e)}\mathsf E_RN\longrightarrow\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}N$$
is a natural derived-system morphism
$$b^{\rm sys}_N:\mathsf T_X^{(e)}\mathsf E_RN\longrightarrow\mathsf E_S\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}N.$$
It satisfies $\epsilon^{\rm sys}_{S,\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}N}\circ\mathsf F_S(b^{\rm sys}_N)=\lambda_N$ as an identity of entire systems. Its evaluation at $n$ is the $F_{B_n}\dashv G_{B_n}$ transpose of $T_{Y,n}(\epsilon_{A_n,N_n})\circ\alpha_{n,G_{A_n}N_n}^{-1}$, where $T_{W,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_n}B_n$. The quotient transitions of this morphism are those induced by the finite exceptional quotient comparisons of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] and the finite-free coefficient squares; the construction retains their quotient cocycles and the finite unit/counit identities. No uniform interval in $n$ is assumed for $N$, and no lift determined solely by finite evaluations is asserted.

proof.text:
Use [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] on the actual map of ring systems $A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$. It constructs $\mathsf T_W^{(e)}$ on the ordinary derived categories, with the asserted evaluations. Write $Q^A_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$, $Q^B_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$, and let $s_W:Q^B_{m,n}T_{W,m}\xrightarrow\sim T_{W,n}Q^A_{m,n}$ be tensor reassociation. The transition-adjoint is
$$t^{\mathsf T_WN}_{m,n}=T_{W,n}(t^N_{m,n})\circ s_{W,N_m}.$$
Indeed both sides are the scalar-extension adjunct of the strict transition obtained by tensoring the transition of a representative with the quotient $B_m\to B_n$; on tensors it sends $x\otimes b$ to $\tau^N_{m,n}(x)\otimes\bar b$. Associativity of multiplication proves the quotient cocycle before localization. The normalization clause of the current statement of [lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction] supplies the canonical isomorphism $B_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to B_n$ for these actual quotients; no proper/open compositor or its invertibility is used here. Thus $s_W$ and $T_{W,n}(t^N_{m,n})$ are invertible for normalized $N$, proving normalization of $\mathsf T_WN$.

proof.text: For scalar_preserves apply [lem-coef-scalar-systems-normalized] to scalarData and the two actual calculi; this handles exactly the normalization conjunct. For each level n obtain finite freeness of the quotient inclusion by the integral-basis argument of [lem-coef-finite-free-extension], and apply [lem-coef-finite-free-tensor-ctf] to the input level. Transport across scalarEvaluation. This proves the levelwise constructible finite-Tor conjunct without a common interval or Noetherian hypothesis.

proof.text: For the fixed compactification $c=(j,p)$, take the actual system map $c^c_{f,M}=Rp_{*,B}(b_{j,M})\circ a_{p,j_!M}$ of [lem-coef-system-scalar-projection-identification], and call it $\alpha^{\rm sys}_M$. Here $a_p$ is the proper projection transpose and $b_j$ is the open balancing comparison, so this is exactly the comparison specified in the statement. That node proves its invertibility, its realization on simultaneous systems, and that its evaluations are the finite proper-counit/open-balancing maps. [lem-coef-finite-free-compact-composition] identifies those canonical finite-free compact-support comparisons with $\alpha_n$ and supplies their coherent system realization. Both nodes apply to normalized inputs with individually bounded constructible finite-Tor levels, hence to the inputs provided by steps 1–2 and to $\mathsf E_RN$ under the specified system adjunction.

proof.text: All quotient squares here use the actual $A_m\to A_n$ and $B_m\to B_n$ maps. By [lem-coef-system-scalar-projection-identification] the map in step 3 is a specified system map with these transitions. The simultaneous mate construction and evaluation compatibility of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] identify its evaluated transition square with the finite coefficient square. Use the single $R$-basis of $S$ and its reductions stipulated in the first paragraph of [lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction]. In that basis, [lem-coef-system-scalar-projection-identification] identifies the restriction of the comparison with finite-sum distributivity. A quotient sends the coefficient of each basis vector to its residue, so distributing then reducing and reducing then distributing coincide on each summand, also for composite quotients. This describes the already constructed square. The definition of $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ uses only the proper counit and canonical open balancing, not a basis; a different basis computes the same map.

source.place: Finite scalar-extension paragraph: quotient squares and basis-independent normalization

proof.text:
Use the actual adjunction $\mathsf F_S\dashv\mathsf E_S$ stipulated in the statement, with the counit-preserving evaluations of [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates]. In this paragraph its $S$ operations are the stipulated retained levels $en$; no equality of the two uniformizer indices is made. Concretely, it is the adjunction of [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates] for the coefficient field $L$ restricted to the cofinal indices $en$: [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint] constructs the strict-system right adjoint for $S$ with the non-zero-divisor $\pi$, normalized relative to the powers $\pi^nS=v^{en}S$, and states that restricting the $v$-adic construction to this subsequence agrees with it, including its maps. Hence its unit, counit and triangle identities are those of the $v$-adic adjunction at the levels $en$, with composite quotient transitions. Let $\eta_S^{\rm sys}$ be its unit, put $Z=\mathsf T_X^{(e)}\mathsf E_RN$, $H=\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}N$, and form the actual system arrow $\lambda_N:\mathsf F_SZ\to H$ displayed in the statement. Define
$$b_N^{\rm sys}=\mathsf E_S(\lambda_N)\circ\eta^{\rm sys}_{S,Z}.$$
This is the transpose by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; every factor is a morphism of ordinary derived systems. Naturality of the counit and its triangle identity give, within that category,
$$\epsilon^{\rm sys}_{S,H}\circ\mathsf F_S(b_N^{\rm sys})
=\lambda_N\circ\epsilon^{\rm sys}_{S,\mathsf F_SZ}\circ\mathsf F_S(\eta^{\rm sys}_{S,Z})=\lambda_N.$$
For $h:N\to N'$, naturality of $\epsilon_R^{\rm sys}$ and $\alpha^{\rm sys}$ gives $\mathsf T_Y(h)\lambda_N=\lambda_{N'}\mathsf F_S(\mathsf T_X\mathsf E_R(h))$; applying $\mathsf E_S$ and naturality of $\eta_S^{\rm sys}$ proves naturality of $b^{\rm sys}$.

source.place: Finite scalar-extension paragraph, third sentence: transposition through the actual adjunction

proof.text:
The evaluations of the specified system adjunctions preserve finite units and counits by [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates]; their simultaneous enriched realization is [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. Evaluate the formula in step 5 using these specified identifications and the evaluations of step 3. It becomes
$$b_{n,N_n}=G_{B_n}\bigl(T_{Y,n}(\epsilon_{A_n,N_n})\circ\alpha_{n,G_{A_n}N_n}^{-1}\bigr)\circ\eta_{B_n,T_{X,n}G_{A_n}N_n}.$$
This is precisely the finite transpose claimed, not merely a morphism with the same source and target. Evaluating the system counit equation in step 5 gives its finite counit equation with these same maps.

source.place: Finite scalar-extension paragraph: evaluation of the specified exceptional transpose

proof.text:
For clarity write $c^A_{m,n}:Q^A_XG_{A_m}\to G_{A_n}Q^A_Y$ and $c^B_{m,n}:Q^B_XG_{B_m}\to G_{B_n}Q^B_Y$ for the quotient exceptional comparisons (the second uses exponents $em,en$). [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates] gives $t^{\mathsf E_DN}_{m,n}=G_{D_n}(t^N_{m,n})c^D_{m,n}$; [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] identifies these with the canonical finite comparisons. Apply transition-adjoint naturality to the actual system map $b^{\rm sys}$ of step 5 and substitute this formula and the formula of step 1. With $s_W$ as in step 1 and $b_{r,N_r}$ as in step 6, the resulting square is exactly
$$\begin{aligned}
&G_{B_n}\bigl(T_{Y,n}(t^N_{m,n})\circ s_{Y,N_m}\bigr)\circ c^B_{m,n,T_{Y,m}N_m}\circ Q^B_X(b_{m,N_m})\\
&\qquad=b_{n,N_n}\circ T_{X,n}\bigl(G_{A_n}(t^N_{m,n})\circ c^A_{m,n,N_m}\bigr)\circ s_{X,G_{A_m}N_m}.
\end{aligned}$$
Both sides have source $Q^B_XT_{X,m}G_{A_m}N_m$ and target $G_{B_n}T_{Y,n}N_n$. Thus these are exactly the quotient transitions asserted for the finite transposes. Transition-adjoint naturality here follows from the strict-system transition square by the scalar adjunction; it does not use faithfulness of derived evaluations.

source.place: Finite scalar-extension paragraph: explicit quotient square for the exceptional transpose

proof.text: For three indices $r\ge m\ge n$, the actual transition of each constructed system from $r$ to $n$ is its composite through $m$. Substitute the quotient cocycles for $c^A,c^B$ and their identity clauses from [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] in step 7; the two expansions agree under tensor reassociation. This retains the quotient cocycles. The same node gives both finite unit and counit equations; [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates] supplies their identities in the specified system adjunctions. Since step 5 uses exactly those units and counits, none is replaced by an arbitrarily chosen adjunction. All constructions have taken place before any total limit. The cases $m=n$, $E=L$, zero systems and empty schemes reduce to identity or zero maps, and ramification changes only the retained exponents to $en$.
